thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: KV-cache paging rate abnormal (host gpux-12), continuous-batcher pack_size surge, tail P95 latency spike > 3x baseline. Auto-escalation to oncall. link: https://grafana.redwoodinfr.com/d/kv-cache/packers (top panels)
alexa: I'm oncall. paging me to triage. which customers are affected? :eyes:
support-bot: Customers with increased 5xx/timeout counts: acme-payments (production), edgestore (staging). Error types: 504 gateway timeout, infra-queue timeouts. Latest spike started ~14:05 UTC.
sam: grabbing runbook now — triage_kv_cache -> continuous_batching. migrating to #incidents for coordination.
miguel: quick summary: yesterday's packer tweak (PR #4218) lowered min_batch_timeout to 2ms to improve throughput; it increased aggressive packing for mixed-shape workloads. short requests are being starved; packer now aggregates long requests into giant packs causing paging and KV cache blowouts.
danielle: acme-payments reports user-facing errors and order processing delays. Support ticket 5678 logged, CS is waiting for ETA. They flagged ~12% request failures in prod.
alexa: ok plan: (1) apply transient throttle to large requests, (2) revert packer config to previous safe thresholds, (3) enable short-request priority flag and canary the change to one region. volunteers: sam + miguel for patches, maria for rollback if needed.
sam: I can patch the batcher config. propose immediate revert of min_batch_timeout from 2ms -> 8ms and set max_pack_size=64. That should reduce pack sizes and fairness pressure.
miguel: agree. also enable "short_request_priority": true (runtime toggle) to prefer n=1-8 token requests in scheduling.
alexa: add a temporary per-tenant cap for acme-payments to avoid cascading failures (rate limit them to 60% of baseline until stable). danielle coordinate with CS.
maria: preparing revert PR now. patch snippet:
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: continuous-batcher-config
data:
  min_batch_timeout_ms: "8"
  max_pack_size: "64"
  short_request_priority: "true"
```
maria: kubectl apply -f cm-batcher-revert.yaml --namespace=redwood-inference ; rolling restart batcher-deployment -n redwood-inference --timeout=600s
sam: will run patch in prod region-us-east-1 first, canary 5% of machines (label: canary=batcher-fairness). command:
```
kubectl -n redwood-inference set env deploy/batcher GLOBAL_CANARY=us-east-1
kubectl -n redwood-inference rollout restart deploy/batcher --selector=canary=batcher-fairness
```
opsbot: Starting canary rollout for batcher (US-EAST-1) — initiated by sam. job id: deploy-2415678901-canary
miguel: quick metric queries: (promql)
- pack_size_distribution{job="batcher"}
- kv_cache_paging_ops_total[5m]
- request_latency_seconds_bucket{le="0.5"}

miguel: initial observation: pack_size 90th percentile reduced from ~180 -> ~60 inside 2 minutes after revert in canary.
alexa: noticing reduced paging across canary hosts. P95 dropping from ~850ms -> ~210ms. good.
danielle: acme-payments support: initial errors cut by ~60% for the test group — CS notified and will begin partial rollback of customer-side retry logic.
support-bot: Notifying customer point: acme-prod-team@acme.com with incident id IR-2415678901. Template: "We're investigating elevated latency and errors; temporary mitigation in progress." Danielle, sending now?
danielle: sending. cc: @alexa @maria
maria: after 10m canary looks stable. starting rolling rollout to remaining hosts (gradual, 20% increments) with health checks.
sam: monitoring tail latency and kv paging. setting alert thresholds tighter: kv_cache_paging_ops_total > 200/min for >2mins -> page oncall.
alexa: also enabling eviction backpressure: reduce prefetch concurrency to 4 for 15 minutes as extra safety.
miguel: deployed short_request_priority flag across all regions. scheduler logs show fewer pack collisions and fewer large memory spikes.
opsbot: Rollout complete for continuous-batcher: success. all pods ready=99/99. metrics: pack_size_95=58, kv_paging_ops decreased 73%.
alexa: good work. next: prepare hotfix changelog for ops release notes and link to postmortem. assign owners: miguel (root cause analysis), maria (rollback/release notes), sam (monitoring/dashboard updates), danielle (customer comms).
support-bot: CS update sent to acme-payments; they requested ETA for full resolution. we can say: mitigation applied, monitoring, follow-up postmortem within 48h.
maria: logging rollback commit sha: abc1234 -> reverted to abc1220. will open hotfix PR to add safety guard and add unit tests for packer fairness.
alexa: follow-up actions: (1) implement per-tenant pack limits, (2) add regression test to CI for mixed long/short workloads, (3) tune autoscaler to avoid overload-induced paging. create backlog tickets.
miguel: note for postmortem: root cause is aggressive packer config plus workload shift (sudden increase in long-shape requests from edgestore tests) causing cache blowups and eviction storms which cascaded to paging and tail latency.
alexa: closing incident thread. if any regressions after rollback, please reopen thread or page oncall. Postmortem assigned IR-2415678901-POSTMORTEM in /incidents/postmortems. :white_check_mark:
opsbot: Incident closed. Duration: 33m. Actions: rollback config, enable short_request_priority, per-tenant cap for acme-payments. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/IR-2415678901
sam: adding dashboard alerts and a synthetic short-request canary test to prevent recurrence.
